# TechCXO

## Executive summary
TechCXO is an Atlanta-based firm. It calls itself the original pioneer of the fractional C-suite model, and its roster now includes a Fractional Chief AI Officer (CAIO) offer. It sells to businesses from startups to $50M+ in revenue, plus boards and private equity and venture capital firms. It wins on a long track record, a broad bench of operators across every C-level role, and an "operators, not consultants" claim, but it publishes no prices.

## Firmographics
- **Website:** https://www.techcxo.com
- **HQ:** 3423 Piedmont Rd NE, Atlanta, Georgia, 30305, United States. Other offices: Cambridge, Research Triangle Park, Los Angeles and London (KORE1 review, 2026).
- **Size:** Sources disagree.
  - Homepage: 245+ partners and professionals.
  - About page: 125 partners and 150 professionals.
  - PitchBook: 240 total employees.
  - ZoomInfo: 51-200 employees.
  - Zeliq: an estimated 500 employees, which looks too high against the others.
- **Ownership and funding:** Private company. Founders: Kent Elmer and Michael Casey (Crunchbase). Funding amount: Not found. PitchBook lists one investor and an "Accelerator/Inc" deal type, with no figure.
- **Founded:** 2003 (CB Insights says 2004). Formerly known as TechCFO.
- **Primary target:**
  - Growth-stage companies, boards and directors, and private equity and venture capital firms.
  - Claims to have served 7,000+ companies, from venture-backed startups to Global 1000 enterprises.
  - Industries listed on its site: business services, consumer and retail, energy, financial services, healthcare and life sciences, industrials, media, real estate, and technology and software.

## Positioning
- **Hero message:** The homepage shows the headline "Fractional Executives". The page title is "Fractional Executives: Proven C-Suite Leadership for Growth". The AI sub-offer reads: "AI is already inside your business. Without leadership, it stays fragmented."
- **Problem they claim to solve:** AI use is uncoordinated and ungoverned. The CAIO page says AI is "not coordinated, governed, or delivering full value". It also says companies don't necessarily need a permanent Chief AI Officer.
- **Category they claim:** Fractional executive leadership and the "full fractional C-suite". It describes this as a single platform for every C-level function.
- **Recent messaging shifts:**
  - The CAIO is now the featured service on the homepage. The homepage Services block shows only this role.
  - The AI offer is framed around shadow AI. The CAIO page links an Employee AI Usage Survey (PDF dated October 2025).
  - Its AI content also covers sales: a recent post on AI sales enablement and generative engine optimization (GEO), about 14 days old at search time.
  - The homepage now stresses a bench of "200+ partners and principals". The older About page says 125 partners.
  - Exact dates for earlier headlines: Not found.

## Core features
| Offer | Outcome promised |
|---|---|
| AI leadership aligned to business priorities | Clarify where AI can drive the most value in the next 90 days and 12 months, and decide what gets built, adopted, scaled or stopped. |
| Governance and responsible adoption | Governance frameworks for data usage, model oversight and compliance, and a standard way to evaluate and approve AI tools. |
| From experimentation to scalable execution | Pick high-impact use cases and set operating rhythms for testing and expanding AI use. |
| Cross-functional alignment | Align AI efforts across departments and cut duplicate work. |
| Interim leadership and capability build-out | Interim AI leadership, then hand ownership to internal leaders. |

- **Bench add-on:** An accountable CAIO plus an AI bench of architects, data scientists and implementation specialists as needed.
- **Cross-sell:** The same bench covers CFO, CTO, CIO, CMO, CISO, CRO and more, so AI sits next to other roles.

## Pricing and packaging
- **Model:** Retainer-style fractional engagement. The model is inferred from the firm-managed partner model. KORE1 says expect ongoing retainer costs rather than a one-time placement fee.
- **Entry price:** Not published. KORE1 lists "Not published" and "Opaque pricing". Kompella.io, a third party, estimates "Typically $12K-$30K range" as a monthly retainer. That is an estimate, not a TechCXO figure.
- **Savings claim:** The homepage says up to 75% less than a full-time hire.
- **Call to action:** Schedule a 15-minute call.
- **CAIO-specific pricing:** Not found.

## Market sentiment
Customer reviews are thin. The sources below are employee and partner reviews on Glassdoor and analyst roundups, not buyer reviews.

- **What users love:**
  - Glassdoor: 4.8 out of 5 from 22 reviews. A partner praised an "Excellent Financial Model for Fractional Leaders" (Glassdoor, Oct 21, 2025).
  - Third-party view: KORE1 called it a "Category pioneer" with the deepest firm-model bench (KORE1, 2026).
  - Client testimonials appear on the homepage from Logfire, Sikka.ai and Thread. These are self-selected, and the quotes are in videos I could not read.
- **What users complain about:**
  - Partner review: "Little to no support to generate business. You are on your own." (Glassdoor, Sept 4, 2024).
  - Partner review: "Lead generation engine has limits." (Glassdoor, Oct 21, 2025).
  - KORE1 flags a Clutch profile with zero verified reviews and unpublished pricing.
  - No buyer complaints about the CAIO service: Not found.

## Go-to-market
- **Sales motion:** Sales-led. The main call to action is a 15-minute call. The site also uses free guides, a "Free Guide" download, an AI usage survey, case studies and a blog.
- **Content and SEO:** A steady stream of insight posts. Recent titles include AI for brick-and-mortar businesses (07/29/2026) and exit planning for M&A diligence (05/12/2026).
- **Channels:** LinkedIn, YouTube and X are linked from the site.
- **Partners and PE:** Fractional Operating Partners embed in portfolio companies to drive 100-day plans and prepare for exit. A partnership with memoryBlue pairs its revenue leaders with outbound sales execution.
- **Delivery model:** Partners work independently with little overlap, per a former partner. The homepage instead claims a network that moves as a team.
- **Footprint:** Offices in several US cities and London (see Firmographics).

## Where they are weak
- **AI is one of about 13 roles.** The AI page sits among CFO, CMO and other roles. Its AI team members are listed as "AI" or "AI, Product Lead" on the partners page, with no AI-specific credentials shown there.
- **No public pricing.** Buyers can't compare it with a named expert like Acme Advisory before a call.
- **AI sits inside a finance-led firm.** Its ZoomInfo directory shows 77 finance staff against 10 in engineering and technical roles. This is a third-party directory count and may be incomplete.
- **Standards-based governance is not shown.** The CAIO page names governance frameworks for data, model oversight and compliance. It does not mention ISO 42001 or a certification path. Not found on the pages I read.
- **Change management is not the focus.** The CAIO page talks about coordination and decision discipline. It does not name adoption, training or change management for staff.
- **Thin proof for AI.** The homepage lists 20+ case studies, but I did not verify that any are AI engagements. Buyer reviews are scarce, and Clutch has no verified reviews (KORE1).
- **Variable quality.** The partner model means quality can vary between partners (KORE1).
- **Inconsistent size claims.** Headcount figures range from 125 partners to 245+ people across its own pages, which weakens trust in the numbers.

## Assumptions and gaps
- I assumed the page headline "Fractional Executives" is the hero message.
- Funding, revenue, CAIO pricing and AI client results: Not found.
